title: Draft De-anchoring Decoding Does Not Mitigate Contextual Drag in LLM Reasoning

contributions.purpose: Confirms that contextual drag (erroneous drafts in context biasing subsequent generation) is a significant phenomenon.
contributions.mechanism: Measures the accuracy gap between conditioning on correct versus incorrect drafts with explicit verification instructions on Game of 24 with Qwen3-8B.
contributions.evaluation: Accuracy drops by 15.13 percentage points when conditioning on incorrect versus correct drafts.
contributions.source_quote: We confirm that contextual drag is a significant phenomenon: accuracy drops by 15.13 percentage points when conditioning on incorrect versus correct drafts, even with explicit verification instructions.

contributions.purpose: Attempts to mitigate contextual drag without training.
contributions.mechanism: Draft De-anchoring Decoding (D3) maintains dual key-value caches (draft-present and draft-redacted prompts) and interpolates their logits at each decoding step to attenuate harmful anchoring.
contributions.evaluation: Rigorously evaluated on Game of 24 with Qwen3-8B against pre-registered success criteria.
contributions.source_quote: We propose D3, a principled training-free approach based on logit interpolation, and rigorously evaluate it against pre-registered success criteria.

contributions.purpose: Reports that D3 fails to mitigate contextual drag.
contributions.mechanism: Evaluates D3 against two pre-registered criteria: improving wrong-draft accuracy and preserving correct-draft accuracy.
contributions.evaluation: D3 fails both criteria: wrong-draft accuracy -0.65pp (required +5pp) and correct-draft accuracy -2.21pp (allowed -1pp).
contributions.source_quote: We report that D3 fails both criteria: it does not improve wrong-draft accuracy (-0.65pp vs. required +5pp) and loses more than allowed on correct-draft accuracy (-2.21pp vs. allowed -1pp).

contributions.purpose: Explains why decoding-time logit interpolation fails for contextual drag.
contributions.mechanism: Analyzes the draft-absent reference distribution, finding it too weak to serve as a useful reference and unable to distinguish beneficial from harmful anchoring.
contributions.evaluation: Draft-absent logits achieve only ~46% accuracy, too weak to serve as a reference.
contributions.source_quote: We analyze why logit interpolation fails for this task: draft-absent logits are too weak (~46% accuracy), and the method cannot distinguish beneficial from harmful anchoring.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our proposed D3 extends this paradigm to contextual drag mitigation by contrasting draft-present and draft-absent logits.
These successes suggest that a similar approach might mitigate contextual drag from erroneous drafts.
Our work addresses contextual drag specifically in iterative refinement settings where models condition on potentially erroneous drafts.

notes: Explicit negative-result paper (declared in the title): the proposed method D3 fails both pre-registered success criteria. Uses pre-registered evaluation criteria, which is unusual.
